questions.title: Checkpoint 1 - LastLines Procedure
questions.question: Q4(a)
questions.pattern: Read all lines and keep the last N values
questions.task:
4 (a)  A procedure LastLines() will:
• take the name of a text file as a parameter
• output the last three lines from that file, in the same order as they appear in the file.

Note:
• Use local variables LineX, LineY and LineZ to store the three lines from the file.
• You may assume the file exists and contains at least three lines.

Write pseudocode for the procedure LastLines().
expectedThinking: Use a procedure header with filename parameter
Open the file for READ and loop until EOF
Shuffle LineX, LineY, LineZ so the newest line is retained
Output LineX, LineY, LineZ in order

markScheme.criterion: Procedure heading (including parameter) and ending
Declare local line variables and correctly open/close file
Loop to EOF(ThisFile)
Read line from file in loop
Correct line shuffle logic (LineX, LineY, LineZ)
Output the final three lines in correct sequence

assessment.expectedAnswer:
PROCEDURE LastLines(ThisFile : STRING)
DECLARE ThisLine, LineX, LineY, LineZ : STRING
OPENFILE ThisFile FOR READ
LineY <- ""
LineZ <- ""
WHILE NOT EOF(ThisFile)
    READFILE ThisFile, ThisLine
    LineX <- LineY
    LineY <- LineZ
    LineZ <- ThisLine
ENDWHILE
CLOSEFILE ThisFile
OUTPUT LineX
OUTPUT LineY
OUTPUT LineZ
ENDPROCEDURE

questions.title: Checkpoint 2 - MakeNewFile Procedure
questions.question: Q5(a)
questions.pattern: Read grouped records, filter, write to new file, and report counts
questions.task:
A company has several departments. Each department stores the name, email address and status of each employee in its own text file. Employee details are stored as three separate data strings on three consecutive lines.

Module MakeNewFile() is defined to:
• take three string parameters (existing file name, new file name, search status value)
• create a new text file
• write employee details where status is not equal to the search status
• count records in source file and records written
• output a summary.

Write pseudocode for procedure MakeNewFile().
expectedThinking: Open old file for READ and new file for WRITE
Read three lines per employee record in a loop
Compare status line against search status
Write all three lines for matching records
Count copied records and output both counts with file names

markScheme.criterion: Procedure heading/ending with three parameters
Open OldFile for READ and NewFile for WRITE, then close both
Conditional loop to EOF(OldFile)
Read three lines per record in loop
Compare status and write three lines when status does not match
Maintain both counters in loop
Final summary output of both counts and file names

assessment.expectedAnswer:
PROCEDURE MakeNewFile(OldFile, NewFile, Status : STRING)
DECLARE Line1, Line2, Line3 : STRING
DECLARE NumCopied, NumRecs : INTEGER
NumRecs <- 0
NumCopied <- 0
OPENFILE OldFile FOR READ
OPENFILE NewFile FOR WRITE
WHILE NOT EOF(OldFile)
    READFILE OldFile, Line1
    READFILE OldFile, Line2
    READFILE OldFile, Line3
    NumRecs <- NumRecs + 1
    IF Line3 <> Status THEN
        WRITEFILE NewFile, Line1
        WRITEFILE NewFile, Line2
        WRITEFILE NewFile, Line3
        NumCopied <- NumCopied + 1
    ENDIF
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT "File ", OldFile, " contained ", NumRecs, " employee details"
OUTPUT NumCopied, " employee sets of details were written to file ", NewFile
CLOSEFILE OldFile
CLOSEFILE NewFile
ENDPROCEDURE

questions.title: Checkpoint 3 - Save Character Records
questions.question: Q8(b)
questions.pattern: Convert structured records to delimited lines and write file
questions.task:
8  A program is being developed to implement a game for up to six players.

During the game, each player assembles a team of characters. At the start of the game there are 45 characters available.

Each character has four attributes, as follows:

| Attribute | Examples | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Player | 0, 1, 3 | The player the character is assigned to. |
| Role | Builder, Teacher, Doctor | The job that the character will perform in the game. |
| Name | Bill, Lee, Farah, Mo | The name of the character. Several characters may perform the same role, but they will each have a unique name. |
| Level | 14, 23, 76 | The skill level of the character. An integer in the range 0 to 100 inclusive. |

The programmer has defined a record type to define each character.

The record type definition is shown in pseudocode as follows:

TYPE CharacterType
    DECLARE Player : INTEGER
    DECLARE Role : STRING
    DECLARE Name : STRING
    DECLARE Level : INTEGER
ENDTYPE

The Player field indicates the player to which the character is assigned (1 to 6). The field value is 0 if the character is not assigned to any player.

The programmer has defined a global array to store the character data as follows:

DECLARE Character : ARRAY[1:45] OF CharacterType

At the start of the game all record fields are initialised, and all Player field values are set to 0.

The programmer has defined a program module as follows:

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| Assign() | * called with two parameters:\n* an integer representing a player\n* a string representing a character role\n* search the Character array for an unassigned character with the required role\n* If found, assign the character to the given player and output a confirmation message, for example: "Bill the Builder has been assigned to player 3"\n* If no unassigned character with the required role is found, output a suitable message. |

MAIN QUESTION (b)

(b)  A new module will store the contents of the Character array in a text file.

The module is defined as follows:

| Module | Description |
|---|---|
| Save() | * form a string from each record with fields separated by the character "^"\n* write each string to a separate line of the new file named SaveFile.txt |

Complete the pseudocode for module Save().
expectedThinking: Declare local loop/index and line string variables
Build one line per record with ^ separators
Convert numeric Player and Level with NUM_TO_STR
Write each built line then close file

markScheme.criterion: Declare local Index (and Line string) variables
Open SaveFile.txt in WRITE mode and close it
Loop through all 45 elements
Attempt to form output line from all four fields
Correct NUM_TO_STR usage for Player and Level
Correct separator usage between all fields
Write each line to file in loop

assessment.expectedAnswer:
PROCEDURE Save()
DECLARE Index : INTEGER
DECLARE Line : STRING
CONSTANT SEP = "^"
OPENFILE "SaveFile.txt" FOR WRITE
FOR Index <- 1 TO 45
    Line <- NUM_TO_STR(Character[Index].Player) & SEP
    Line <- Line & Character[Index].Role & SEP
    Line <- Line & Character[Index].Name & SEP
    Line <- Line & NUM_TO_STR(Character[Index].Level)
    WRITEFILE "SaveFile.txt", Line
NEXT Index
CLOSEFILE "SaveFile.txt"
ENDPROCEDURE
